plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Whole streets turn lavender-blue as jacarandas flower before their ferny leaves fully emerge. The trumpet-shaped blooms drift down and carpet pavements, cars and lawns in purple.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring in the Southern Hemisphere, from October through late November, with full bloom around November
plants.funFact: Jacarandas are native to South America, but they are now so closely linked with Sydney's spring that the falling flowers are a local tradition. Many people say that a bloom landing on your head brings good luck.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: This glossy-leaved evergreen shrub lights up the cooler months with delicate, open, often lightly fragrant flowers. Their bright petals and golden stamens bloom while most other garden plants are winding down.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn into early winter, typically starting in October or November and continuing through December or January
plants.location: Mild-climate gardens in Japan, where it is native, and the southern United States
plants.funFact: Sasanqua camellias are close relatives of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis. The seeds of some camellias are pressed for a prized culinary and cosmetic oil.

plants.name: Nerine bowdenii
plants.description: When the autumn garden has faded, slender bare stems rise from the soil and carry heads of ruffled, spidery pink flowers that glisten as if dusted with tiny crystals. They stand out against the muted tones of late autumn.
plants.location: Gardens in the United Kingdom, from a native range in South Africa's Drakensberg mountains
plants.funFact: Nerines flower on naked stems before their strap-like leaves grow. They bloom best when their bulbs are crowded and baked in sun, so they are often planted at the foot of a sunny wall.
